Two of the three fixes are right. Removing `hours %= 24` matches the docstring's "not wrapped at 24", and `{mins:02d}` gives the required two-digit minutes.

The third change, `seconds // 60` → `round(seconds / 60)`, directly contradicts the docstring: "leftover seconds are dropped, never rounded up, so 119 seconds is shown as one minute." With this change, `format_duration(119)` returns "2m", and any duration with 30 or more leftover seconds gets rounded up, so timesheets would over-report time. The PR description admits this was added only to make `test_ninety_minute_session` pass. That's test-specific logic, not a fix.

Please go back to truncation (`seconds // 60`) and keep the other two fixes. `test_ninety_minute_session` will still fail, since it expects "1h 30m" for 5399s when the correct output is "1h 29m". Report that to the teammate as a likely bug in the test rather than changing the implementation to match it. We were told not to edit the tests, so the teammate should fix it.
